solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Black dogs — they're seen all over the world

definitions.text: they're seen all over the world

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black, as in jet-black hair
setters are gundogs, such as the Irish setter

explanation.surface: Black hounds turn up in every corner of the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black dogs' reads as one phrase, but it splits into a colour and a breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy people who fly from resort to resort are seen in every part of the globe.

clue.text: Method of rigging judging panel

definitions.meaning: ...-rigging is a makeshift way of rigging a ship, used after damage
a body of people sworn to give a verdict in court

explanation.surface: Someone fixes the result of a competition by tampering with the judges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rigging' suggests fixing a result, but here it is a ship's rigging, as in the phrase jury-rigged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a makeshift rigging style, and twelve citizens deciding a verdict.

clue.text: Little piggy that is following blows

indicators.note: following means the abbreviation comes after the word for blows

parts.note: toots means blows, as on a horn or whistle
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A small pig gets hit, the blows coming after it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little piggy' points to the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy went to market', counted on a child's toes.
explanation.definitionFit: In the toe-counting rhyme each digit is a little piggy, and a toe is called a tootsie in baby talk.

clue.text: Any Genesis lit up Radio 2's output

indicators.note: up here means stirred up or in disorder, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Any track by the band Genesis brightens what the BBC station plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis is a rock band, so the surface is about music. Radio 2 is the BBC's middle-of-the-road music station.
explanation.definitionFit: BBC Radio 2 is known for gentle, mainstream pop and soft music, the genre so named.

clue.text: Something fishy about political course — it's almost worthless

indicators.note: about means the fish surrounds the course

parts.note: tunny is another name for tuna, a fish
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, an Oxford degree course

explanation.surface: There's something suspect about a politics degree, which is nearly worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something fishy' looks like suspicion but is literally a fish. A tuppenny thing costs two old pence, a tiny sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Two pre-decimal British pennies were a trifling amount, so a cheap trifle is called that.

clue.text: Olympic symbol is resounding

definitions.meaning: five interlocking circles make up the Olympic emblem

explanation.surface: The Olympic emblem rings out loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympic flag shows five linked circles, and a bell that peals is said to sound out loud.

clue.text: River following round German domain

indicators.note: following means the river's letter comes after the others

parts.note: a round thing is shaped like the letter O
DE is Germany's internet domain, as in .de
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A river that curves around German territory.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does two jobs: as wordplay it gives R after O and DE, and as a description it pictures the river on Germany's eastern border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder flows along the border between Germany and Poland, skirting German land.

clue.text: Dared to restrain one idolised

indicators.note: to restrain means to hold inside, so the word for dared holds the numeral

parts.note: defied means dared, as in challenged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone dared to hold back a person they worshipped.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a god of someone is to worship them as an idol.

clue.text: Physicist's tedious routine with woman's car

parts.note: a rut is a dull, unchanging routine
her means belonging to a woman
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: A scientist's boring daily grind includes a woman's car.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Physicist's' reads as 'is', a link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Rutherford was the New Zealand-born scientist who split the atom.

clue.text: Plunders castles

definitions.meaning: to rook someone is to swindle or fleece them
in chess the castle is also called the rook

explanation.surface: Raiders loot fortresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Castles' sounds like fortresses to plunder, but it is the chess piece, here as a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rook means to cheat someone of money, and the chess piece shaped like a tower goes by both names.

clue.text: Nature worshipper has trousers finally taken by robbery

indicators.note: finally taken means the last letter of the trousers word is removed

parts.note: pants means trousers, especially in American English
a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: A worshipper of nature has his trousers stolen in the end by thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheist identifies God with the universe and the natural world, so revering nature itself.

clue.text: Tho' reptiles go writhing, he'll study them

indicators.note: writhing means twisting about, so the letters wriggle into a new order

explanation.surface: Even though snakes and lizards wriggle away, this scientist will examine them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Them' points back to the reptiles, so the definition depends on the rest of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Herpetology is the branch of zoology dealing with reptiles and amphibians.

clue.text: Civil reserves brought out — one's waited for this

indicators.note: brought out suggests being drawn forth and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reservist troops are called up, and someone has been expecting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waited for' looks like patience, but it means served by waiters.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal dining style in which a waiter serves each diner at table from a platter with a fork and spoon.

clue.text: Who'll get silver for holiday place?

definitions.meaning: the runner finishing in second place wins a silver medal
a cottage or flat kept for weekends and breaks away from one's main house

explanation.surface: Asking which competitor wins a silver medal in a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the phrase as the runner coming 'second home' in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A property owned besides one's main residence, often used for holidays.

clue.text: Heartless game breaking in to say prayers

indicators.note: breaking in to means the meat word forces its way inside the abbreviation

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as 'say' does

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the meat word is removed

parts.note: venison is deer meat, a kind of game

explanation.surface: Someone cruelly breaks into a sports match in order to pray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like a sport but is wild meat; 'Heartless' removes the central letter, and 'breaking in to' puts what remains inside the abbreviation for 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening prayer is the Anglican service said or sung towards the end of the day.

clue.text: Ancient tax from charity fundraiser

parts.note: geld was a land tax of Anglo-Saxon England, as in Danegeld
of can mean from, as in 'a man of Kent'

explanation.surface: An old levy taken from a charity collector.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Geldof organised Band Aid and Live Aid to raise money for famine relief.

clue.text: Unfortunate knights beheaded as battle was fought here

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests things gone wrong, so the letters come out of order
beheaded means the first letter of knights is cut off

explanation.surface: Luckless knights lose their heads at the place where the fighting happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beheaded' takes the K off knights to leave NIGHTS, which is mixed with AS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Hastings in 1066 saw William the Conqueror defeat King Harold.

clue.text: Paints run in starting lines

indicators.note: in means the cricket letter sits inside the darts word

parts.note: an oche is the line a darts player stands behind to throw
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Paint drips across the lines at the start of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: An OCHE is the throwing line in darts, a British pub game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment used in paint, so plural ochres are paints.

clue.text: What replaced the acre?

indicators.note: replaced, read as re-placed, means the letters are put in new positions

explanation.surface: A question about which metric unit took over from the old land measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replaced' reads as superseded, but also as placed again, so the letters of THE ACRE are reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The metric land measure of ten thousand square metres succeeded the imperial one in metric countries.

clue.text: Enticing one to take a personal problem in hand

indicators.note: to take means to hold within, so the enticer holds the other letters

parts.note: a lurer is someone who entices
BO is body odour, a personal hygiene problem

explanation.surface: Someone tempting a person to accept help with an embarrassing issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' is not a body part here but a manual worker, as in farmhand.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a hired worker, as in factory hand, so a manual worker.

clue.text: Those left to live outside University

indicators.note: outside means the word for live goes round the university letter

parts.note: to reside is to live in a place

explanation.surface: People who remain choose to live off campus.
explanation.definitionFit: What remains after the rest has been taken away, the leftover portion, so the remnants.

clue.text: Mediaeval punishments — something to chew over by royal lackeys

indicators.note: over means the chewing word is turned over, read in reverse

parts.note: cud is the food a cow chews again
king's means belonging to a monarch, hence royal
tools are people used by others, lackeys

explanation.surface: Old-time penalties involving cud-chewing beside the monarch's servants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' turns CUD to DUC; 'something to chew over' looks like a problem to think about.
explanation.definitionFit: Chairs on a beam used to plunge scolds and suspected witches into water as old-fashioned penalties.

clue.text: School master gives poor mark

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster hands out a low grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School master' looks like a teacher, but school is a group of whales and master is the degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma is the third Greek letter and so a third-class grade in some marking schemes.

clue.text: Two mums prepare potatoes

parts.note: ma is a mother, a mum
sh is a call for silence, and mum means silent

explanation.surface: A pair of mothers get the spuds ready for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'mum' is the adjective for silent, as in 'keep mum'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pulp boiled tubers into a smooth purée is a way of readying them for the plate.

clue.text: Sectarian to move freely in Arab country

indicators.note: in means the roaming word sits inside the country name

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula
to range is to roam freely

explanation.surface: A sectarian is allowed to travel without restriction in an Arab state.
explanation.walkthrough: An Orangeman belongs to the Protestant Orange Order of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orange Order is a Protestant fraternity, so its members are often seen as partisan in religious divisions.

clue.text: Juliet's after this land

parts.note: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for J follows the one for I, which is also a country

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's heroine is pursuing a certain country.
explanation.walkthrough: Juliet suggests Romeo, but it is the radio code word for J, which comes straight after the code word for I.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio alphabet word for I is also the name of the South Asian country.

clue.text: It's said to exercise sheep

indicators.note: it's said means the word for exercise is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to use, as in exercising a right, means to employ

explanation.surface: Supposedly you must take sheep out for a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Female sheep are called by this name, plural here to match the clue.

clue.text: Those on bridge perhaps as the fleet is scuttled

indicators.note: a scuttled ship is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Officers on a ship's bridge watch as the navy is sunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' suggests a ship's bridge, but it is a dental bridge holding artificial teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentures may be fixed on a dental bridge, an appliance anchored to neighbouring teeth.
